thread:
alicia: :rotating_light: Seeing sustained 503s from hosted inference across multiple customers hitting /v1/generate since ~09:03 UTC. P50 latency jumped, p95 spiking. Customers reporting timeouts. Paging SRE.
raj: On it, joining war room. Can someone grab recent gateway and runtime logs?
mike: I see a sharp increase in concurrent requests and a backlog on the batcher queues. Possibly autoscaler didn’t spin up fast enough.
deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-176451. Notifying oncall.
raj: repro attempt (local):
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood-hosted.example/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","prompt":"test","max_tokens":64}'
```
(alicia: curl returns HTTP/1.1 503 and connection reset)
support: 3 customers have escalated via support@ with traces showing 503 + client timeouts (timeouts after 30s). Sharing customer IDs in DM.
alicia: quick log extract from runtime (relevant lines):
```
2026-03-17T09:03:12Z runtime batcher: enqueue request id=abcd conn=23
2026-03-17T09:03:12Z runtime batcher: start batch size=64 queue=120
2026-03-17T09:03:14Z kernel: allocate kv cache failed: OOM?
2026-03-17T09:03:15Z gateway: upstream returned 503, code=EPIPE
```
mike: looks like memory pressure on a subset of GPUs causing kernel failures -> batcher stalls -> gateway 503s. Two quick mitigations: 1) reduce max_batch_size for affected pool, 2) re-route traffic to fallback quantized model (rwd-small-1-q4) to reduce memory.
raj: Doing mitigation 2 now: toggling policy to route non-SLA traffic to rwd-small-1-q4.
deploy-bot: Routing config updated (route-id rt-773) -> fallback enabled.
alicia: After reroute p95 errors dropped from ~18% to ~2% in 3m. Customers still seeing occasional 503s but much lower.
mike: Also increasing Dedicated pool for hosted-runtime by +2 nodes (temp). Kicking a scale-up.
deploy-bot: Scale-up requested; new nodes provisioning.
raj: Temporary circuit-breaker: enable 503-backoff policy for /v1/generate at edge to reduce amplification.
support-bot: Notified affected customers with status page link and short mitigation note.
support: Customer-facing message approved: "We observed elevated 503s due to runtime memory pressure; we routed affected traffic to a lower-memory model and scaled capacity. We're monitoring; next update in 30m."
alicia: Good. Taking incident notes: root cause hypothesis = intermittent kv-cache OOMs under bursty batch sizes + delayed autoscaler reaction.
raj: Action items (short):
- raj: investigate root cause of kernel kv-cache OOMs, collect coredumps (due 2026-03-20)
- mike: tune autoscaler warmup & add buffer for batcher pools (due 2026-03-24)
- infra: add alert for batcher queue length > 80% for >2m (due 2026-03-18)
- eng-runtime: add graceful fallback at kernel layer to reject oversized batches earlier (due 2026-04-01)
- support: follow up with customers individually with RCA when ready (due 2026-03-22)
alicia: scheduling postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 PST. Invite: svc-incident, eng-runtime, infra, support.
mike: quick note — postmortem should include memory regression checks and recent kernel changes (look at commit range abc123..def456).
raj: will attach timeline + logs to INC-176451. Thanks everyone for quick response. :thumbsup:
alicia: Closing war room for now; monitoring in progress. Reopen if errors climb above 5%.
support: Acknowledged. Will update customers after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
